quests.summary: Elder Bai wants the Blood Moon War chronicles copied before anything else goes missing from his shelves.

dialogue.speaker: elder_bai
dialogue.text: My spectacles are back, and I can see again, which means I can see how much work there is.

dialogue.speaker: elder_bai
dialogue.text: I want every scroll that mentions the Blood Moon War copied, twice, and hidden in two places. Humour an old man.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The pagoda's fourth floor smells of dust and camphor. A gap on the east shelf shows where something was taken.

objectives.text: Copy the war chronicles in the quiet pavilion

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You copy until your wrist aches. The chronicles praise the Azure Cloud's founder, and mention an ally only once, as 'our green friends'.

dialogue.speaker: elder_bai
dialogue.text: 'Our green friends.' Always that phrase. Someone went to great trouble to make a whole sect into a footnote.

dialogue.speaker: elder_bai
dialogue.text: Put your copy behind the turtle soup recipes. Nobody ever reads those. Except me.

quests.title: Wolves Under the Wall
quests.summary: Howling again, beyond the outer pines. The wolves are thin, frightened, and closer to the sect than wolves should be.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Beyond the outer pines, three wolves watch you with ordinary grey eyes. Not red. Only hungry, and afraid of something behind them.

objectives.text: Break the spirit wolves at the outer pines

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Drive them off, don't kill them if you can. Their eyes are clean. Something chased them here.

objectives.text: Look for Han Xue at the quiet pavilion

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They came from the bamboo forest. Whatever was feeding the wolf king blood, the rest of the pack remembers it.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: The deacon's dead. Who's still doing it?

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: That's the right question. Keep asking it quietly. Some people in this sect dislike questions.

objectives.choice_prompt: The spirit wolves were driven mad by a demonic talisman nailed to a tree.

choices.text: Burn the talisman and calm the beasts

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: You're too nice. It's annoying. I like it.

choices.text: Take it to the elders as evidence

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Rules, rules. Fine. You're right. Again.

choices.text: Keep it. It could be useful.

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Remind me never to owe you money.

quests.title: Contribution by Kindness
quests.summary: The sect is short-handed with the Medicine Hall's apprentice away on the herb caravan. Chores pile up in odd places.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Xiao Man has gone south with the herb caravan for the season, and I've discovered she did the work of three.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: I need the drying racks turned. I need the moonbell fed. Please don't ask what moonbell eats.

objectives.text: Meet Lu Ping at the gate post

dialogue.speaker: gate_lu
dialogue.text: You're doing Xiao Man's chores? She waters the gate lanterns, you know. I never asked why. Now you can.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Why does she water the lanterns?

dialogue.speaker: gate_lu
dialogue.text: Luck, she says. And nothing's attacked the gate since she started. Mostly nothing.

objectives.text: Talk with Elder Mo at the hall steps

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Eleven points for a ferret, four for puppets, six for the Medicine Hall. You're climbing the stele.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Hmph. Don't grin. The stele is stone. It doesn't care, and neither do I.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: ...I'm told I'm grinning. I'm not. Go away.

quests.title: A Letter Under the Door
quests.summary: Someone else slid a letter under the Sect Master's sealed door. Elder Mo found it, and does not like the handwriting.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Your report went under her door. So did another, this morning. Unsigned, and folded in the Law Hall's way.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: I don't read other people's letters. I read the envelopes. This one smelled of blood lotus.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Faint footprints lead from the sealed doors toward the scholar rock and the Law Hall beyond, then vanish on swept stone.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The gold seal is intact. Your pendant warms as you pass it, as if the doors were breathing on the other side.

objectives.text: Talk it over with Han Xue

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Law Hall folding and blood lotus. Might mean nothing. The Law Hall handles evidence, and evidence smells.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Might mean something. Tell no one but Elder Mo. And me. You've told me, so that's done.

quests.title: The Bell Nobody Rang
quests.summary: At midnight the gate bell sounds once, then stops. Lu Ping swears he didn't touch it. Something is testing the wall.

dialogue.speaker: gate_lu
dialogue.text: I didn't ring it! I was asleep. I mean, meditating. The bell rang itself, once, and then the pines went quiet.

dialogue.speaker: gate_lu
dialogue.text: Quiet like a held breath. I hate that kind of quiet.

objectives.text: Ring the gate bell to wake the watch

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The bell booms. Lanterns flare along the wall, and in the pines something that was creeping forward stops, and turns.

objectives.text: Stop the spirit wolves at the outer pines

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Grey wolves come out of the dark, and behind them, a pair of eyes the colour of old blood that does not come closer.

objectives.text: Find Wei Tong after the fight

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: Those eyes at the back. Red. Like the wolf king's. It didn't fight. It watched.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: It counted us. Like Hong counted graves.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: I didn't need that thought tonight. I'm going to sleep with Dumpling under my pillow.

objectives.choice_prompt: Behind the spirit wolves you drove off, a den of whimpering pups.

choices.text: Carry them to the deep forest, far from people

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: You're too nice. It's annoying. I like it.

choices.text: Report the den to the sect's beast keepers

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: By the book. The Law Hall would weep with joy.

choices.text: Sell the pups to a beast trader

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: (quietly) That was cold, {player}. Even for a war.

quests.title: The Stele Remembers You
quests.summary: Your points are enough for a cultivation manual and an hour at the formation's edge. Qi gathers faster than it did in spring.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Enough points for a manual. Choose the Cloud-Step Breathing. It is boring. Boring is how you get strong.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Go and sit on the stone bridge. Don't come back until your breath is longer than your excuses.

objectives.text: Refine your cultivation at the stone bridge

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The Cloud-Step Breathing is boring, exactly as promised. Your qi does not care. It gathers, and gathers, and rises a level.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: When you open your eyes, the pond is full of stars, and your meridians feel like rivers after rain.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Middle stage. Adequate. Back straight, though. The pond saw you slouching.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Mm.

bonus.note: Grateful people press medicine into your hands.
Frightened people pay you to go away. You take it.
The Law Hall records your conduct with approval.
Rules bent, lessons learned the hard way.

quests.title: Baskets for the Bamboo
quests.summary: Elder Hua is taking the Medicine Hall to the bamboo forest for the autumn harvest, and you have been volunteered as a mule.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: (sighs) I can see the precepts sliding off you like rain.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Punctual, correct, precepts in order. You make an old teacher's work easy.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Twelve baskets, three disciples, one forest. The moonbell sprouts are ripe and they won't pick themselves. They bite, remember.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Wei Tong has gone ahead to 'scout'. That means he's found somewhere to eat. Find him.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: And if he's eaten the baskets?

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Then you'll carry the herbs in your robe. Go on.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The forest path is carpeted in gold leaves. It is almost peaceful, if you forget the last time you walked it.

objectives.text: Find Wei Tong at the forest path

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: I scouted. The mushrooms by the stream are delicious. Well, one was. The other was educational.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: The grove's further in. I didn't want to go alone. Not after last time. Let's go together.

objectives.choice_prompt: Wei Tong mentions a junior stealing food from the kitchens for a sick friend.

choices.text: Cover the food yourself

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: You're too nice. It's annoying. I like it.

choices.text: Report it; the kitchens have rules

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: By the book. The Law Hall would weep with joy.

choices.text: Tell the junior you'll stay quiet, for a price

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: (quietly) That was cold, {player}. Even for a war.

quests.title: Ash on the Moonbell
quests.summary: The herb grove's moonbell is spotted with grey ash that smears like blood when you touch it.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Half the moonbell in the grove is spotted grey. When you rub the spots, your fingers come away red.

objectives.text: Join Elder Hua at the herb grove

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Blood qi, in the soil. The grove is drinking it up from somewhere deeper.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Healthy ones in this basket, sick ones in that one. Don't eat either. Wei Tong, I'm looking at you.

quests.title: Tea With the Hermit
quests.summary: The hermit of the bamboo is expecting you. He has poured three cups, which is one more than there are of you.

objectives.text: Make your way to the hermit's hut

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Three cups of tea steam on the hermit's step. He looks at your baskets, then at the grey ash on your fingers.

objectives.text: Share your findings with the hermit

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: Ash on the moonbell. Ah. The den still bleeds, then. Old wounds in the earth close slower than in people.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: The wolf king's den? The wolf king is dead.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: The wolf is. The blood they poured into him is not. It soaked down, and down, and is still looking for a way up.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: The third cup is for your Elder Hua. She never drinks it. I keep pouring. That is what hope looks like at my age.

quests.title: The Den Still Bleeds
quests.summary: Down in the old wolf den, the rock weeps red. Something has moved in to drink from it.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The wolf den breathes warm air. Red water seeps from cracks in the rock and pools in the hollows.

objectives.text: Defeat the corrupted wolves at the wolf den

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: Wolves. Red-eyed ones. I thought we'd seen the last of these. Dumpling, wake up!

objectives.text: Collect the blood-soaked earth for Elder Hua
Tell Wei Tong what you found

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: They weren't a pack. They were just... drinking. Like moths at a lamp.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Then we put out the lamp.

objectives.choice_prompt: One of the corrupted wolves lies wounded, panting, its eyes clearing now that the fight is over.

choices.text: Bind its leg and let it limp away

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: That's why people follow you, you know.

choices.text: Give it a clean, quick end

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: Fair enough. Can't argue with that.

choices.text: Cut out its core while it still breathes

reply.speaker: senior_wei
reply.text: Remind me never to owe you money.

quests.title: Roots in the Red Rock
quests.summary: The blood seeps from a seal carved deep in the den, far older than the wolf king and nothing like Keeper Hong's work.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: At the back of the den a round seal is carved into the rock: a moon swallowing a sword, ringed with runes worn nearly smooth.

objectives.text: Gather the loose rune chips around the seal
Scrub the blood-rune seal with the hermit's salt

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The salt hisses. Red runs out of the grooves. For a moment the seal glows green at its edges, answering your pendant.

objectives.text: Drive the corrupted wolves from the herb grove

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Somewhere in the grove behind you, the last of the drinking wolves howl, and come.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: In the clearing the air smells clean for the first time today. Even the bamboo seems to stand up straighter.

quests.title: Salt, Sutras and Silence
quests.summary: The hermit says the seal must be quieted with a still heart, not a sword. He means yours.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: The Blood Moon carved that seal three centuries ago, to bleed this forest slowly. Somebody has been feeding it again.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: A sword would crack it. A quiet heart will close it. Go and sit beside it, and be very dull for an hour.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Wei Tong says I'm good at being dull.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: Your friend is wise in unexpected directions.

objectives.text: Still your heart beside the spirit spring

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You breathe with the spring. Far off, deep in the den, a knot in the earth loosens, and the red in the water thins to nothing.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: Closed. For now. The forest thanks you. It thanks you by not trying to eat you tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: All right.

quests.title: Bandits at the Harvest
quests.summary: Scavengers from Iron-Fang's broken gang have smelled the Medicine Hall's baskets. Rare herbs sell well in the lowlands.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Senior Sister Han Xue, reporting for basket duty. Elder Mo sent me. He said you'd find trouble within the hour.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Bandits on the path. Six. They want the herbs. I want them to leave. Let's see who's more persuasive.

objectives.text: Clear the forest path of bandits

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: More bandits? Heaven must think we're bored.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: More on the bridge! These ones have Iron-Fang's red headbands. The gang didn't scatter as far as we hoped.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The bandits flee downstream, leaving one sandal and a very small, very old basket of stolen herbs.

quests.title: What the Bandit Said
quests.summary: One bandit was too slow to run. He is young, frightened, and says something about families that nobody in the sect wants to hear.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: This one was too slow to run. He's younger than you. He keeps saying the chief made them do it.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Ask him. He won't talk to me. I apparently look like I bite.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The young bandit won't meet your eyes. They took my mother, he whispers. Iron-Fang says if we don't pay, she doesn't eat.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Who took her? Iron-Fang?

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Not him. Them. The ones with the red moon. He shakes and says no more, and Han Xue lets him run home.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: Families held against good behaviour. That is how they did it three hundred years ago, too. Some recipes never change.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: Take your herbs home, child. And your questions. Keep the questions somewhere safer than the herbs.

objectives.choice_prompt: The young bandit is still tied up outside the hut, waiting to learn what you'll do with him.

choices.text: Let him go to warn his family

reply.speaker: hermit_lan
reply.text: Mercy costs something. You paid it without complaint. Well done.

choices.text: Deliver him to the magistrate

reply.speaker: hermit_lan
reply.text: Correct. The precepts exist for moments like this.

choices.text: Beat the rest of the truth out of him

reply.speaker: hermit_lan
reply.text: (a long silence) I did not teach you that.

quests.title: Moonbell Wine
quests.summary: The harvest is in. Elder Hua allows exactly one cup of moonbell wine, and the hermit finally drinks his tea.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: The grove is healing, the baskets are full, and not one of my disciples was bitten. By moonbell. I count wolves separately.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Fetch the spring water for the wine. One cup each. I will be counting, and so will the moonbell.

objectives.text: Fill the flasks at the spirit spring
Pour the first cup at the ruined shrine

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You pour a cup onto the stones of the old shrine. A breeze turns the bamboo toward you, and the shrine's cracked lotus carving seems to lean closer.

objectives.text: Hear what the hermit has to say

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: She drank the tea. Forty years I've poured that cup. She drank it and called it bitter.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Is that good?

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: It's a beginning. The bitter ones always are.

quests.title: Carry It Home
quests.summary: The Medicine Hall returns with full baskets and one worried Elder. On the road back, Elder Hua asks what the bandit said.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Han Xue says one of those bandits spoke to you. Families held hostage. By the Blood Moon.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: I've mended bandits before. They always said they had reasons. I never listened. I wonder now how many were true.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: We'll tell Elder Mo, and the Sect Master when she comes out.

objectives.text: Meet Wei Tong at the lookout rock

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: I carried four baskets. Four! Elder Hua gave me one dried persimmon for my trouble.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: It was a very good persimmon. I'd carry four more. Don't tell her.

bonus.note: Grateful people press medicine into your hands.
Frightened people pay you to go away. You take it.
The Law Hall records your conduct with approval.
Rules bent, lessons learned the hard way.

quests.title: No Salt in Qingshi
quests.summary: Qingshi has had no salt for a month. Constable Du asks the sect for help, and Elder Mo sends you and Han Xue down the mountain.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Qingshi has had no salt in a month. Bandits on the road. The Sect Master is still sealed away, so I'm sending you.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Han Xue goes too. Don't argue. She's a better cook and a worse liar than you.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Qingshi's gate is open, but the market beyond it is half empty. A child is licking a salt-lick meant for oxen.

objectives.text: Talk with Constable Du at the town gate

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Cultivators. Good. Salt's gone, tempers are short, and last night someone boiled seawater they don't have.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Caravans vanish on the forest road. Iron-Fang's leftovers, the carters say. Led by a man with a scar like a canal.

objectives.choice_prompt: A dead courier's satchel holds silver for Blood Moon informers, and their names.

choices.text: Burn the names; they were desperate

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: Most cultivators wouldn't have. Thank you.

choices.text: Give the names to the magistrate

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: Proper. Very proper. Good.

choices.text: Keep the silver

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: (nervously) Y-yes. Of course. Whatever the immortal wishes.

quests.title: Tallies at the Warehouse
quests.summary: Merchant Jin keeps the guild's salt tallies. He is nervous, overdressed, and suddenly very keen to be helpful.

dialogue.speaker: merchant_jin
dialogue.text: The immortal who helps! My grandmother lit incense for you.

dialogue.speaker: merchant_jin
dialogue.text: Salt, salt, everybody asks me about salt. The guild lost four caravans. Four! I'm practically a victim.

dialogue.speaker: merchant_jin
dialogue.text: Here, look at the tallies. Every wagon, every weight. I've nothing to hide. Please stop looking at my crates.

objectives.text: Make your way to the guild warehouse

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The warehouse yard is stacked with empty salt barrels. Somebody has scrubbed the stamps off half of them.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The tallies are neat and honest, except for one column, marked with a crescent, where the numbers are far too round.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: A crescent. Same as Hong's ledger. Jin is still selling to somebody who signs with a moon.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Not now. We can't prove anything and we need his wagons. But I'm writing it down. In ink.

quests.title: Gossip Is Also Salt
quests.summary: Madam Fang's customers complain about the food, the bandits, and the magistrate, in that order.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: My noodles taste of nothing and my customers taste of complaints. Bring back the salt, immortal, and eat free.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: The carters drink here. They say the bandits don't take the salt. They take the salt and the carters. Then send the carters home.

objectives.text: Find Old Pan at the docks

dialogue.speaker: ferryman_pan
dialogue.text: Seen them. From the river. They camp in the old bandit camp in the bamboo, the one you burned last spring.

dialogue.speaker: ferryman_pan
dialogue.text: Came back like weeds. They're thinner now. Hungrier. Hungry men are dangerous and sad in equal parts.

objectives.text: Join Magistrate Zhou at the yamen

dialogue.speaker: magistrate_zhou
dialogue.text: The yamen has issued a strongly worded proclamation. It is nailed to the gate. It uses the word 'forthwith' twice.

dialogue.speaker: magistrate_zhou
dialogue.text: I, ah, have also put forty guards on the road. That was Constable Du's idea. The proclamation was mine.

objectives.choice_prompt: Magistrate Zhou admits the town's grain tally was fudged to feed the refugees.

choices.text: Keep it quiet. It fed people.

reply.speaker: magistrate_zhou
reply.text: Most cultivators wouldn't have. Thank you.

choices.text: Insist the books be put right

reply.speaker: magistrate_zhou
reply.text: Proper. Very proper. Good.

choices.text: Take a cut for your silence

reply.speaker: magistrate_zhou
reply.text: (backing away) As you say, immortal.

quests.title: Guarding the Last Caravan
quests.summary: The last salt caravan of the season leaves the forest road at dusk. The bandits will not let it pass quietly.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Last caravan of the season comes out of the bamboo at dusk. If it doesn't reach the gate, the town goes hungry.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: I've six men and a very old spear. You're the rest of the plan.

objectives.text: Ring the caravan bell at the gate

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The caravan bell clangs. Out on the road, wagons creak into a run, and shapes rise out of the ditches on either side.

objectives.text: Break the salt-road bandits at the terraced fields

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They're on the fields! Get between them and the wagons!

objectives.text: Stop the salt-road bandits at the main street

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Salt-road bandits spill out of cover, weapons bright.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Every barrel's in. Not one carter hurt. I'm going to write this down in the good ink.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: They weren't fighting to kill. They wanted the carters alive.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Then I'll ask the carters what they were for. Quietly, over a cup of Madam Fang's awful tea.

quests.title: The Carter Who Came Back
quests.summary: A carter taken last week walked home with a message pinned to his coat. It is addressed to the sect.

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: He came to the well at dawn, the carter. Walked like a man asleep. There was a letter pinned to him.

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: I read it. I shouldn't have. It isn't for me. It's for you.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The carter sits by the well, staring at nothing, a folded paper pinned to his coat with a bandit's knife.

objectives.text: Read the letter pinned to the carter

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Sect brats. Stay out of the bamboo, and the salt comes back. Come in, and my men stop being gentle. Gou.

objectives.text: Show Han Xue what you found

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Gentle. They call that gentle. The man doesn't know his own name.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: He's afraid of something bigger than us. That's the only reason a bandit writes letters.

quests.title: Tracks Toward the Bamboo
quests.summary: The carters' tracks lead off the road and into the forest, toward the camp you burned in spring.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Wheel ruts leave the road at the river and turn toward the dark line of bamboo on the far bank.

objectives.text: Defeat the salt-road bandits at the forest path

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Lookouts drop from the bamboo with sharpened poles. They are thin, and frightened, and very determined.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: From the lookout rock you can see the old camp rebuilt: tents, fires, and a pen full of silent carters.

objectives.text: Talk it over with Han Xue

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They're holding the carters. Feeding them, even. Like livestock.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Or like hostages. Someone's holding their families. Now they're holding ours.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Then we take them all home. Carters first. Answers second. The scarred man last.

quests.title: The Pen of Carters
quests.summary: Before Gou can move his prisoners, you slip into the camp at night to open the pen.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The pen is a ring of stakes and rope. Inside, a dozen carters sit very still, listening to the fires.

objectives.text: Drive the salt-road bandits from the old bandit camp

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Left side's mine. Right side's yours. Middle is whoever's faster.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The ropes part. The carters don't run at first. They've forgotten how. Then one laughs, and they all run at once.

objectives.text: Share your findings with Han Xue

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They're out. Gou isn't in the camp. His tent is empty and warm.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: He'll be back, and angry. Angry men are sloppy. Let's be the opposite.

quests.title: A Scar Like a Canal
quests.summary: Gou's tent holds maps, a child's wooden toy and a list of names. The names are not his victims.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Gou's tent is neat as a soldier's. A map of the salt road, a carved wooden horse, and a long list of names.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Beside each name: a village, and the words 'held since'. Beside the last name: Gou's own mother. Held since spring.

objectives.text: Tell Han Xue what you found

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They're not stealing salt. They're paying a ransom with it. Salt, carters, whatever the moon asks for.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: The Blood Moon has their families. Just like the young one said.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: This goes to Elder Mo. And the Sect Master, when she opens that door. I'm starting to hate that door.

quests.title: Gou the Scarred
quests.summary: Gou the Scarred returns to find his camp empty and his hostages gone. He has nothing left to bargain with, and nothing to lose.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Torches below. Gou the Scarred is back, and he is not shouting. He is very quietly sharpening a blade on the empty pen.

objectives.name: Gou the Scarred
objectives.text: Face Gou the Scarred at the old bandit camp

dialogue.speaker: bandit_gou
dialogue.text: You took my carters. Do you know what that costs me? Not silver. Not salt. My mother's dinner.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Then help us get her back instead. We're not the ones holding her.

dialogue.speaker: bandit_gou
dialogue.text: Nobody gets them back! Nobody! Pick up your sword, sect brat!

objectives.text: Catch your breath with Gou the Scarred

dialogue.speaker: bandit_gou
dialogue.text: Why... didn't you kill me?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Because you're not the one I'm angry at. Give Constable Du your men's names. All of them. And the villages.

dialogue.speaker: bandit_gou
dialogue.text: ...You're a fool. Iron-Fang would've gutted you. Fine. Fine. Names. For whatever good it does.

objectives.choice_prompt: Gou sits in the dirt, beaten, his men's names half-written. The carters he took want him punished.

choices.text: Spare him, and send him with the names to Du

reply.speaker: bandit_gou
reply.text: Soft. Soft wins more fights than people think.

choices.text: Hand him to Constable Du for judgement

reply.speaker: bandit_gou
reply.text: Rules. You sects and your rules. ...It was the right call.

choices.text: Break his sword hand so he never raids again

reply.speaker: bandit_gou
reply.text: Careful. I know where that road ends.

quests.title: Salt on the Table
quests.summary: Qingshi has salt again. Madam Fang's noodles taste of something, and Gou sits in the yamen cell writing names.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: Salt! Noodles that taste like noodles! Free bowls for the heroes. Two each. I'm feeling reckless.

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: Constable Du has the scarred one writing in the yamen. Page after page. Villages I've never heard of.

objectives.text: Sit in the quiet of the town temple

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: In the clean temple, you breathe. A page of names drifts through your mind. Every name is somebody's mother.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Your qi steadies around the thought, and deepens. Not anger. Something slower, that will last longer.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Forty-one names. Forty-one families held by the Blood Moon. The magistrate fainted. Then he got up and sent letters.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: I don't know where they're kept. But now I know they exist. That's how every case starts.

bonus.note: Grateful people press medicine into your hands.
Frightened people pay you to go away. You take it.
The Law Hall records your conduct with approval.
Rules bent, lessons learned the hard way.

quests.title: Notices on Every Pillar
quests.summary: The examination notices have gone up. Lu Ping has already opened a betting book, and the odds on you are insulting.

dialogue.speaker: gate_lu
dialogue.text: (bows three times, then a fourth to be safe) {senior}! Sorry. You're very high up now. It's hard not to bow.

dialogue.speaker: gate_lu
dialogue.text: Examination in five days! Precepts, puppets, pills and a bout. I've opened a book. You're at six to one.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Six to one? Who's the favourite?

dialogue.speaker: gate_lu
dialogue.text: Zhao Kang, obviously. Two to one. He's been training at night. Very dramatically. With his shirt off.

objectives.text: Make your way to the formation plaza

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Examination banners hang around the plaza. A list of rules is pinned to every pillar. Rule one: no bribing the puppets.

objectives.text: Hear what Zhao Kang has to say

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: Come to look at the banners? Look well. You'll see my name on the top one soon enough.

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: Don't embarrass yourself, village brat. It reflects badly on the whole outer court. On me, specifically.

quests.title: The Ninth Precept
quests.summary: Elder Gu will test the Nine Precepts himself. He has never been known to pass anyone who stumbled on the ninth.

dialogue.speaker: elder_gu
dialogue.text: The written examination is mine. Nine precepts, recited and explained. Most disciples stumble on the ninth.

dialogue.speaker: elder_gu
dialogue.text: Guard the seal, even unto death. Tell me, disciple. What seal?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I don't know, Elder. Nobody will tell me.

dialogue.speaker: elder_gu
dialogue.text: Good. An honest ignorance. Go and read the stele again. Then come back and tell me what it means to you.

objectives.text: Study the ninth precept on the stele

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Guard the seal, even unto death. The words are worn smooth by generations of fingers. Yours join them.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I think it means some things are worth more than the one guarding them.

dialogue.speaker: elder_gu
dialogue.text: ...Yes. That is what it means. It is also what it costs. Pass. Go. Go, disciple.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: For a moment Elder Gu looks very old. Then the Law Hall's cold returns to his face, and he waves you out.

quests.title: The Puppet Gauntlet
quests.summary: Wei Tong runs the puppet gauntlet this year, and has tuned the puppets to 'mildly offended'.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: You've changed. I haven't decided if I like it.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: The hero of the hour! Stop blushing. Everyone's talking about you.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: The gauntlet! Five puppets, one after another. I've tuned them to mildly offended. Last year was enraged. We lost a wall.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: No elbows. No weeping. No hitting me, even if I deserve it.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: Here they come. Strike first, apologise never.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: Clean run! Zhao Kang did it faster, but he knocked one puppet's head into the lotus pond. Points off for littering.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: You're neck and neck. Elder Hua's pill test is next. That one I can't help you with. I once made a pill that exploded.

quests.title: A Pill Worth Passing
quests.summary: Elder Hua's test is simple: refine one Qi-Gathering Pill that doesn't explode. You'll need the right herbs first.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: One Qi-Gathering Pill. Three kinds of herb, one clean fire, and a hand that doesn't shake. Gather your own herbs.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Last year three disciples picked moonbell instead of mountain sage. They're fine now. They can almost whistle again.

objectives.text: Pick mountain sage on the terraces

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Mountain sage. Correct. Now the fire. Breathe. The cauldron can hear panic.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The pill rolls out round and pale green, and smells faintly of rain. Elder Hua sniffs it and nods once.

dialogue.speaker: elder_hua
dialogue.text: Pass. Zhao Kang's pill was perfect. Also, it had his clan's crest pressed into it. Show-off.

objectives.choice_prompt: Your pill cracked a little at the edge, and Elder Hua didn't notice.

choices.text: Point out the crack yourself

reply.speaker: elder_hua
reply.text: Correct. The precepts exist for moments like this.

choices.text: Say nothing. A pass is a pass.

reply.speaker: elder_hua
reply.text: Hm. Measured. I can live with measured.

choices.text: Swap it for a spare from Zhao Kang's tray

reply.speaker: elder_hua
reply.text: The precepts weep. I'll pretend not to hear them.

quests.title: The Night Before the Bout
quests.summary: The bout is at dawn. Han Xue gives advice, Elder Mo gives none, and Zhao Kang gives you a look you can't read.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Zhao Kang favours his left. He was taught by expensive masters, and they all had the same bad habit.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Also, get some sleep. You look like a ghost that's worried about exams.

objectives.text: Meet Elder Mo at the hall steps

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Advice? No. You know how to fight. The question is whether you know how to lose. Everyone should, once.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I don't intend to lose, Elder.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Nobody intends to. Hmph. Sleep.

objectives.text: Talk with Zhao Kang at the plum garden

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: I heard what Elder Gu said to you. About the ninth precept. He passed you. He's never passed anyone on the ninth.

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: My brother was the last one who came close. Never mind. Tomorrow I'll beat you properly. Sleep well. I mean it.

objectives.choice_prompt: Zhao Kang asks what you really think of the sect's precepts.

choices.text: They keep us from becoming the Blood Moon

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: Rules, rules. Fine. You're right. Again.

choices.text: Kindness first. Precepts after.

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: You're too nice. It's annoying. I like it.

choices.text: They're tools. Use them when they help you.

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: Rules are for people without your luck.

quests.title: Zhao Kang at Dawn
quests.summary: The final bout of the examination: you and Zhao Kang, on the formation plaza, in front of every outer disciple.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Bout of the outer examination! Zhao Kang against {player}! Wooden swords, clean strikes, no clan politics!

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: Wooden swords. How quaint. Don't cry when I win.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Zhao Kang's attendants insist on 'assisting their young master'. Fine. Beat them too. Begin!

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: Draw. Elder Mo called it a draw. A draw! I had you at the second exchange.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: You had me at the fourth. I had you at the fifth.

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: Hmph. Fine. A draw. The first time a draw hasn't felt like losing. Don't read anything into that.

quests.title: Results on the Stele
quests.summary: The results are carved at the gate, and your name sits where nobody expected it to sit.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A crowd at the stele. Your name is carved third from the top, level with Zhao Kang's. Lu Ping is weeping into his betting book.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: First: a quiet girl from Cloud Peak who nobody bet on. Joint second: Zhao Kang, and you.

dialogue.speaker: gate_lu
dialogue.text: Six to one! I had three stones on you and two on Zhao Kang. I've won and lost at the same time. Is this enlightenment?

dialogue.speaker: gate_lu
dialogue.text: And the Cloud Peak girl! Nobody bet on her. Nobody even knew her name. It's Qiu Ling, by the way. I asked. Late.

quests.title: Gu Hanshan's Question
quests.summary: Elder Gu summons you to the Law Hall after the results. He wants to know about your pendant, and about Qingshi.

dialogue.speaker: elder_gu
dialogue.text: Third place, and the ninth precept. You interest me, disciple. So does your report on Qingshi. It reached me too.

dialogue.speaker: elder_gu
dialogue.text: The deacon spoke of your pendant before he died. What did he say? Exactly.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: That the Patriarch would be pleased with him. Then that he is coming for me.

dialogue.speaker: elder_gu
dialogue.text: Dying men say many things. Keep that jade close, and your mouth closer. The Law Hall will see to the rest.

objectives.text: Find Han Xue at the quiet pavilion

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: He asked about the pendant? Before he asked about the deacon?

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: It's nothing. It's his job. I'll keep telling myself that until it stops being true.

objectives.choice_prompt: Han Xue asks you to vouch for a friend's examination, though you've never seen their work.

choices.text: Vouch anyway

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Ha! The elders are going to hate that. I love it.

choices.text: Refuse. Vouching must be honest.

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: By the book. The Law Hall would weep with joy.

choices.text: Vouch, for a favour later

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: (quietly) That was cold, {player}. Even for a war.

quests.title: Lanterns for the Passing
quests.summary: Every disciple who passed floats a lantern from the cliff edge. It is tradition, and slightly dangerous.

dialogue.speaker: elder_bai
dialogue.text: Word of your conduct travels. All of it good. Sit.

dialogue.speaker: elder_bai
dialogue.text: The Lantern of Passing. Write what you want from your cultivation on the paper, then let the wind take it.

dialogue.speaker: elder_bai
dialogue.text: Mine said 'more shelves'. Sixty years ago. Heaven has a slow delivery service.

objectives.text: Collect paper lanterns from the plaza
Release your lantern over the sea of clouds

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Your lantern drifts out over the sea of clouds with a hundred others. You wrote: to be strong enough to protect people.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Beside you, Zhao Kang's lantern says: to beat you. Beneath it, in smaller writing: and to make my brother proud.

objectives.text: Join Zhao Kang at the plum garden

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: Don't read other people's lanterns. It's the worst manners in the sect. What did yours say? No. Don't tell me.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Thank you.

quests.title: Late Autumn, Late Stage
quests.summary: Examination over, you have earned a month in the cultivation caves. Elder Mo walks you there himself.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: A month in the caves. Your first. No food, no talk, no Wei Tong. Heaven's gift to you.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: If you open your eyes before the month is out, you'll find me outside, disappointed.

objectives.text: Cultivate in seclusion above the clouds

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Days fold into each other. Your qi wears smooth grooves in your meridians, and deepens them, and deepens them again.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: On the last morning you open your eyes. Elder Mo is outside, asleep sitting up, a blanket on his knees.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: I was not sleeping. I was guarding. Late stage of Qi Condensation? Adequate.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: The Sect Master stirs, they say. Not yet. Soon. Go and eat something.

bonus.note: Grateful people press medicine into your hands.
Frightened people pay you to go away. You take it.
The Law Hall records your conduct with approval.
Rules bent, lessons learned the hard way.

quests.title: Invitation From the Yamen
quests.summary: Magistrate Zhou writes to the sect: Qingshi holds its Ghost Festival for the lost, and the town would like its heroes there.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: The magistrate's written. The town's holding the Ghost Festival for everyone the new moon took. They want us there.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: I said yes. Then I realised I have to be polite for a whole day. Come with me. You're better at polite.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Paper lanterns hang from every eave in Qingshi. Children fold boats from red paper. The whole town smells of incense and fried dough.

dialogue.speaker: magistrate_zhou
dialogue.text: The heroes of Qingshi! Welcome, welcome. I have prepared a speech. It is only nine pages.

dialogue.speaker: magistrate_zhou
dialogue.text: Constable Du says I should cut it to one. Constable Du has no poetry in his soul.

quests.title: Paper Boats and Names
quests.summary: Widow Liu is folding a paper boat for her son, and asks you to write his name on it. She can't bring herself to.

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: (starts to kneel, then catches themself) Heavens. You feel like weather now, did you know?

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: Every boat carries a name down the river to the ones we lost. I've folded one for Liu Er.

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: I can't write it. My hand won't. Will you? You found out what happened to him. You should.

objectives.text: Buy lantern oil in the market for the boats
Launch Liu Er's boat on the river

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You write Liu Er in your neatest hand. The boat turns once in the current, as if looking back, then drifts away.

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: He's not dead. I know you think he's not. I only let the boat go because the town expects it.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Then let it carry a message instead. We're coming.

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: ...Yes. That's better. That's a much better boat.

quests.title: The River Won't Take Them
quests.summary: The paper boats are drifting back to shore, upstream, against the current. Old Pan has never seen anything like it.

dialogue.speaker: ferryman_pan
dialogue.text: Forty years on this water and I've never seen boats come back. Upstream. Against the current.

dialogue.speaker: ferryman_pan
dialogue.text: The river's refusing the names. Or something under it is.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Dozens of paper boats bob against the bank, pressed there by a current that runs the wrong way.

objectives.text: Touch the backward current with your qi

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Cold, and a pull downward. A thread of old blood qi runs along the riverbed toward the hill graves.

objectives.text: Show Han Xue what you found

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Hong's circle. We broke it. We didn't dig it out. Some of its roots must run under the river.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Festival or not, we have to look. Quietly. Nobody wants a panic at a funeral.

quests.title: Things in the Reeds
quests.summary: Something drags itself out of the reeds after dark, drawn by the festival lanterns and the living warmth of the town.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The festival lanterns reflect on black water. Among the reeds, eyes. Many eyes, low to the ground.

objectives.text: Clear the docks of spirit wolves

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Wolves! Soaked, starving, and blood-drunk. Keep them away from the boats, the children are still out!

objectives.text: Gather the lanterns the wolves scattered
Talk it over with Constable Du

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Wolves, in town, during the festival. I'm going to have to write a very long report.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Thank you. The children didn't see. Well, they saw. They think it was a play. They want it again tomorrow.

objectives.choice_prompt: The spirit wolves were driven mad by a demonic talisman nailed to a tree.

choices.text: Burn the talisman and calm the beasts

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: Heaven bless you, immortal. We won't forget.

choices.text: Take it to the elders as evidence

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: The magistrate would approve. So do I.

choices.text: Keep it. It could be useful.

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: (nervously) Y-yes. Of course. Whatever the immortal wishes.

quests.title: Roots Under the Graves
quests.summary: Beneath the hill graves, the blood-ink circle you broke is dry. But something new has been dug beside it.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The old rune circle is grey dust. Beside it, fresh earth, and a new trench running downhill toward the river.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Your palm meets the runes and they fizz like wet fuses. The trench goes dark, and far below you the river sighs.

objectives.text: Fight off the Blood Moon cultivators

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Robed figures rise from behind the tombs, masks painted with red moons. They were waiting for someone to come.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The street is bright with lanterns again. Nobody noticed. Somewhere behind you, the river begins to flow the right way.

quests.title: The Mask That Stayed Behind
quests.summary: One of the masked cultivators dropped a mask as he fled. Inside it, someone has written a name, and a date.

objectives.text: Make your way to the hill graves

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A cracked red mask lies among the graves. Inside, in neat brush strokes: the next new moon. Qingshi. Again.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The ink is fresh. Not Hong's hand; this writer is younger, and in a hurry. Beneath the date, a crescent.

objectives.text: Share your findings with Han Xue

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They're not finished with this town. Hong was one deacon. There are others, and they have calendars.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Then the town needs more than a festival. It needs watchers.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: It needs the Sect Master to open that door. I'm going to write her another letter. A rude one.

objectives.choice_prompt: The dropped mask names its owner, a Qingshi fishmonger. The constable hasn't seen it.

choices.text: Take it to Constable Du

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: By the book. The Law Hall would weep with joy.

choices.text: Warn the fishmonger first; maybe he was forced

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: That's why people follow you, you know.

choices.text: Keep it, and make the fishmonger work for you

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: (quietly) That was cold, {player}. Even for a war.

quests.title: Watchers for Qingshi
quests.summary: Qingshi needs its own eyes. The ferryman, the innkeeper and the constable volunteer. So, surprisingly, does Merchant Jin.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Watchers. Yes. I can put men on the gate and the tower. The river is harder.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: On my way.

objectives.text: Hear what Old Pan has to say

dialogue.speaker: ferryman_pan
dialogue.text: The river? I'm on it day and night anyway. I'll watch. Fare's free for this one.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I hear you.

objectives.text: Meet Madam Fang at the Drunken Crane

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: Everybody tells me everything eventually. It's the wine. I'll send word up the mountain if anyone new asks about the graves.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I won't forget it.

objectives.text: Talk with Merchant Jin at the guild warehouse

dialogue.speaker: merchant_jin
dialogue.text: The guild has pigeons. Fast ones. For prices. They could carry other messages. For a fee. A small fee. No fee. Fine.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Thank you, Master Jin.

dialogue.speaker: merchant_jin
dialogue.text: Don't thank me. It makes me nervous. People only thank me before bad news.

quests.title: The Night of Lanterns
quests.summary: On the festival's last night the whole town walks to the river with lanterns. The masked cultivators choose that moment.

dialogue.speaker: magistrate_zhou
dialogue.text: My speech! I'm about to give my speech! Nine pages! Why are there men with swords on the rooftops?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I'll be quick.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The bell rings out over the river. Lantern-bearers scatter to the doorways, just as masked figures drop into the street.

objectives.text: Break the Blood Moon cultivators at the main street

dialogue.speaker: magistrate_zhou
dialogue.text: Stay close! I am not writing to your family.

objectives.text: Stop the Blood Moon cultivators at the market square

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They're after the crowd! Keep them in the square. Nobody gets dragged anywhere tonight!

dialogue.speaker: magistrate_zhou
dialogue.text: I gave my speech. All nine pages. Behind a barricade. To seven people and a goat. It was my finest hour.

dialogue.speaker: magistrate_zhou
dialogue.text: Thank you, immortal. The town saw you stand in the square. They'll remember that longer than my speech.

quests.title: Incense for the Lost
quests.summary: When the lanterns are gone, Widow Liu asks you to burn incense at the temple for everyone still missing.

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: Burn one for Liu Er, and one for every name the scarred bandit wrote down. There's a lot of names.

dialogue.speaker: widow_liu
dialogue.text: Heaven keeps its accounts. So do I. So should you, I think.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Forty-one names from Gou's list, and eleven from Qingshi. You burn one stick for each. The temple fills with slow grey smoke.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Your qi settles into the silence like a stone into deep water.

objectives.text: Find Madam Fang at the Drunken Crane

dialogue.speaker: innkeeper_fang
dialogue.text: You look like you need wine. You're getting tea. Tea is for people who have more work tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Yes.

quests.title: Back Up the Mountain
quests.summary: The festival is over. Han Xue walks you to the town gate with a letter for the Sect Master and a very long face.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: My letter to the Sect Master is four pages. Three of them are just the word 'please'.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Word from the sect, too. The outer disciples are being sent into the Moonlit Grotto. It opens once a decade.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: A secret realm? Now?

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Elder Mo says it's exactly now. The sect needs strong disciples, and the grotto makes them. Or eats them. Mostly makes them.

objectives.text: Join Constable Du at the town gate

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: Safe road, immortals. The watchers are set. The town will hold till you're back.

dialogue.speaker: constable_du
dialogue.text: And if it doesn't, I'll write it down. Then I'll hold it anyway.

objectives.choice_prompt: Constable Du asks you to settle a farmers' quarrel. One of them is your friend.

choices.text: Judge it fairly

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: Proper. Very proper. Good.

choices.text: Favour the poorer one

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: Heaven bless you, immortal. We won't forget.

choices.text: Favour whoever pays

reply.speaker: constable_du
reply.text: (nervously) Y-yes. Of course. Whatever the immortal wishes.

bonus.note: Grateful people press medicine into your hands.
Frightened people pay you to go away. You take it.
The Law Hall records your conduct with approval.
Rules bent, lessons learned the hard way.

quests.title: Once a Decade
quests.summary: Elder Mo gathers the chosen disciples at the teleport array: the Moonlit Grotto opens tonight, beneath the old wolf den.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: The Moonlit Grotto opens once a decade, under the bamboo. Disciples go in, disciples come out stronger. Usually.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Han Xue leads. Wei Tong carries the food. Zhao Kang carries his mouth. You carry that pendant, and bring it back.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Why the pendant, Elder?

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Because it glows when it's near old things, and the grotto is very old. Go.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Where the blood seal once wept, the rock has split, and silver light pours out of the crack like water from a jar.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: In we go. Stay together. The grotto moves its rooms around. Last decade a disciple came out two weeks late and very confused.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Yes. I think so too.

quests.title: The Tablet of Rules
quests.summary: Just inside the grotto a tablet lists its rules. Most of them are warnings. One of them is a joke. You hope.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Inside, the forest is the forest, but silvered, as if the moon had soaked into every leaf. The sky is a stone ceiling.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Take nothing that is not offered. Harm nothing that does not harm you. Do not eat the silver peaches. We mean it.

objectives.text: Tell Wei Tong what you found

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: Silver peaches? There are silver peaches? Where? Just to know where not to go.

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: He's going to eat the peaches.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: He's going to eat the peaches.

quests.title: Moonlit Herbs
quests.summary: The grotto's herbs grow in minutes and fade in hours. Han Xue wants a basket before the light changes.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Moon-sage. It only grows here. Elder Hua would give a year of her life for a basket of it.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Pick fast. They wilt when the grotto shifts, and it shifts often.

objectives.text: Pick moon-sage in the silvered grove

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: A full basket. Good. Did Wei Tong eat a peach?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Half a peach.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Then we have about an hour before something very large comes to complain.

quests.title: The Peach Keepers
quests.summary: Something very large comes to complain about the peach.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: It was half a peach! Half! It was mostly pit! Who's coming? Why is the ground shaking?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I'll handle it.

objectives.text: Defeat the stone golems at the herb grove

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: Stone golems. Wonderful. Wei Tong, next time, starve.

objectives.text: Finish the stone golems at the clearing

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The last golem crumbles. From its rubble rolls a single silver peach, which Wei Tong looks at, then very bravely does not touch.

quests.title: Rivals Among the Silver
quests.summary: You are not the only sect in the grotto. Rogue cultivators have slipped in through the crack, and they are not following the rules.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Tents in the silver forest. Rogue cultivators, a dozen of them, digging up everything that glows.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Sacks of moon-sage torn up by the roots. Carved tablets smashed for their jade. A map, with the grotto's heart marked in red.

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: Tomb raiders. Grave robbers with swords. They'll strip this place bare.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They're heading for the heart. So are we. Now it's a race.

objectives.choice_prompt: Something valuable lies here, unclaimed: a purse of spirit stones.

choices.text: Report it to the sect

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: Rules, rules. Fine. You're right. Again.

choices.text: Leave it for whoever lost it

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: You're too nice. It's annoying. I like it.

choices.text: Pocket it quietly

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: Rules are for people without your luck.

quests.title: Rules of the Grotto
quests.summary: The rogue cultivators have found the grotto's guardians too, and are losing badly. They'd like to take you down with them.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: They woke the guardians and ran toward us. That's a tactic. A cowardly, effective tactic.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Right away.

objectives.choice_prompt: One of the rogues who woke the guardians is pinned under fallen stone, begging.

choices.text: Free him and send him out

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: That's why people follow you, you know.

choices.text: Free him, and tie him up for the wardens

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: By the book. The Law Hall would weep with joy.

choices.text: Leave him for the guardians

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Remind me never to owe you money.

objectives.text: Drive the rogue cultivators from the old bridge

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A shout goes up. The rogue cultivators have found you first.

objectives.text: Cut down the stone golems that follow

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: Rogues on the left, golems on the right. I'll take the rogues. They're uglier.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: When the dust settles, the surviving rogues are gone, and the path to the grotto's heart stands open beneath a silver arch.

quests.title: Around a Silver Fire
quests.summary: The grotto's night is short and bright. Around the fire, your companions say things they wouldn't say in daylight.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: When I was small, I wanted to be a cook. My father said cultivators eat better. He was wrong. Cultivators eat faster.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: I'm still going to open a noodle shop one day. The Dumpling. Named after my sword. Or the other way round.

objectives.text: Hear what Zhao Kang has to say

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: My brother came to this grotto ten years ago. He came out first. My father had it carved on a stone in our hall.

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: I'm going to come out first too. Not for my father. For the stone. It looks lonely.

objectives.text: Meet Han Xue at the spirit spring

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: I don't have a story. I have a sword and a senior sister's responsibilities. Go to sleep, all of you.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Senior Sister, you're smiling.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: It's the fire. Silver fire. Very misleading. Sleep.

quests.title: The Silver Arch
quests.summary: Beyond the arch the grotto grows old: carved pillars, faded murals, and a green that is not quite moonlight.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The arch is carved with flowers so worn you can't tell what they were. Your pendant warms. Just slightly.

objectives.text: Gather the fallen tiles of the arch
Set the tiles back into the arch

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The last tile clicks home. For a heartbeat every carved flower flushes green, then fades back to silver.

objectives.text: Clear the ruins courtyard of stone golems

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The floor shivers, and the grotto's stone keepers rise to see who has touched their arch.

objectives.text: Make your way to the ruins courtyard

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Beyond the keepers lies a quiet courtyard, silver on green, and a sound like distant water.

quests.title: The Flower Nobody Remembers
quests.summary: A mural in the grotto's heart shows a sect in green robes. The paint has been scraped from every face.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A mural covers the wall: cultivators in green robes, holding flowers. Every face has been scraped away, carefully.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Only one flower remains untouched in the corner: a lotus, carved exactly like the jade at your belt. Your pendant is warm as a hand.

objectives.text: Show Han Xue what you found

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Someone came in here with a knife and took their time. Why scrape faces off a painting?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: So nobody remembers them.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: That's what I'm afraid of. Don't touch it. We tell Elder Mo. Keep your pendant under your robe.

objectives.choice_prompt: A sealed jade slip lies here, stamped with another sect's seal.

choices.text: Return it to its sect unread

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Rules, rules. Fine. You're right. Again.

choices.text: Read it first. Knowledge is knowledge.

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Ha! The elders are going to hate that. I love it.

choices.text: Sell it to the highest bidder

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Remind me never to owe you money.

quests.title: Moonlight in the Marrow
quests.summary: At the edge of the grotto's heart a spring of silver qi bubbles up. Han Xue stands guard while each of you takes a turn.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: One at a time. The spring is strong. Too much and you'll be seeing silver for a week. Wei Tong goes last.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: Why me last?

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Because you ate the peach.

objectives.text: Bathe your meridians in silver qi

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Silver qi floods your meridians, cool as moonlight on water. Everything you have gathered this year settles, and brightens.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Behind your eyes the green lotus from the mural opens, once, and closes, like a door you are not yet allowed through.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Ninth layer of Qi Condensation. I can see it in the way you're standing. Don't let it go to your head.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: The heart is ahead. Something is guarding it. It has been guarding it for a very long time.

bonus.note: Grateful people press medicine into your hands.
Frightened people pay you to go away. You take it.
The Law Hall records your conduct with approval.
Rules bent, lessons learned the hard way.

quests.title: The Rogues Come Back
quests.summary: The rogue cultivators have regrouped with friends, and they have brought picks for the grotto's heart.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Torches at the silver arch. The rogues are back, twice as many, with picks and chains and one very large hammer.

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: They're going to break the arch! Barbarians! That's at least a thousand years of carving!

objectives.text: Recover the jade the rogues pried loose
Talk it over with Zhao Kang

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: They ran. Again. They're very good at running. I should learn it. Tactically.

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: The one with the hammer said something about the warden's treasure being worth a city. What treasure?

objectives.choice_prompt: One of the rogue cultivators is still alive, clutching a wound and begging for his life.

choices.text: Bind his wound and let him go

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: That's why people follow you, you know.

choices.text: Hand him over to face the law

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: By the book. The Law Hall would weep with joy.

choices.text: End it. He would have killed you.

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: (quietly) That was cold, {player}. Even for a war.

choices.text: Make him swear to serve you, then let him run

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: Ha! The elders are going to hate that. I love it.

quests.title: A Question in Stone
quests.summary: Carved over the heart's door is a single question, repeated in seven scripts. Only one of them you can read.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A door of green stone, and above it one question carved in seven scripts. You can read only the last.

objectives.text: Read the question over the door

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Who carries the flower? And beneath, smaller: if no one, go home. If someone, wake me gently.

objectives.text: Share your findings with Han Xue

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Who carries the flower. It means you, doesn't it. Your pendant hasn't stopped glowing since the arch.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I don't know what it means. But it's the same flower.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Then we don't wake it. Not yet. Not until we know what gently means to a stone.

objectives.choice_prompt: A spirit crane is caught in a poacher's snare nearby.

choices.text: Free it and bind its wing

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: That's why people follow you, you know.

choices.text: Report the poachers to the sect

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: By the book. The Law Hall would weep with joy.

choices.text: Take it for its feathers

reply.speaker: senior_han
reply.text: Remind me never to owe you money.

quests.title: Counsel From Outside
quests.summary: A paper crane flies in through the grotto's crack, carrying a note from the hermit, who seems to know where you are.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A paper crane circles your head and lands on your hand. It unfolds into a note in a spidery, ancient hand.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The warden asks a question. Answer it honestly, and it will test you. Lie, and it will bury you. Bring tea. The Hermit.

objectives.text: Talk with Wei Tong at the clearing

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: Bring tea? To a fight? The hermit is very strange. I respect it.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: I have tea. I have everything. I packed for a war and a picnic, just in case.

objectives.text: Find Zhao Kang at the lookout rock

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: How does a hermit know where we are? How does a hermit send cranes into a secret realm?

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: The older I get, the less I understand old people.

quests.title: Stones for the Door
quests.summary: The door to the heart has seven empty sockets. The seven stones are scattered where the grotto last shifted.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Seven sockets. Seven stones, and the grotto moved them around to be difficult.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: You can count on me.

objectives.text: Find the seven door-stones in the clearing
Break the spirit wolves at the clearing

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Grey wolves with silver-tipped fur lope out of the long grass, guarding the stones like shepherds.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Seven stones. The wolves only wanted to see if we were polite. We were. Mostly.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I'll remember.

quests.title: Tea for a Giant
quests.summary: You set the stones and pour a cup of Wei Tong's tea at the door, feeling ridiculous. The door opens anyway.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You set the seventh stone and pour a cup of tea at the threshold. It feels ridiculous. The door opens.

objectives.text: Pour tea at the warden's door

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Inside, a giant of green stone kneels with its head bowed over a sword. Moss has grown over its shoulders like a cloak.

objectives.text: Tell Wei Tong what you found

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: It's asleep. It's very big and very asleep. Can we leave it like that? I vote we leave it like that.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Whatever it guards, the rogues will be back for it. We can't leave it like that.

quests.title: The Grotto Warden
quests.summary: The warden wakes, and asks its question with its fists.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The warden lifts its head. Moss sloughs away. A voice like millstones: who carries the flower?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: I do. I don't know what it means. But I carry it.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Honest. Good. Show me the flower has roots.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The warden kneels again, and opens its stone hand. In it lies a slip of green jade, warm, and a single seed of a lotus.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: Not yet, it grinds. The rest when you are ready. It closes its eyes, and is moss again.

objectives.text: Join Han Xue at the forest path

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: It gave you a seed and a slip, and went back to sleep. That's the strangest treasure I've ever heard of.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: The slip is blank. The seed is just a seed.

dialogue.speaker: senior_han
dialogue.text: Then they're for later. Put them with your pendant. Everything strange seems to belong together.

quests.title: The Grotto Begins to Close
quests.summary: With the heart given up, the grotto starts to fold shut. The rogues make one last grab on the way out.

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: The walls are moving! The grotto's closing! Everyone to the crack, now!

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Of course. I'll see what I can find.

objectives.text: Stop the rogue cultivators at the clearing

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The rogues burst out of the silver trees, desperate, hammers raised, grabbing at anything that glows.

objectives.text: Make your way to the wolf den

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: You tumble out of the crack into ordinary bamboo, ordinary daylight. Behind you the rock closes like a mouth.

quests.title: Who Came Out First
quests.summary: Out in the bamboo, the other teams are waiting, counting heads. Zhao Kang wants to know who came out first.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The other teams wait on the forest path, counting heads. The monitor elder is marking a list with great ceremony.

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: Who came out first? I need to know. For the stone. Tell me it was me.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: It was you, Zhao Kang. By a whole step. I saw it.

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: ...You're lying. You were in front of me. You stepped back. Why would you do that?

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Your brother's stone looked lonely.

dialogue.speaker: rival_zhao
dialogue.text: ...Don't. Don't be kind to me. It's unbearable. Thank you.

objectives.choice_prompt: The grotto's prize token is in your pocket. By rights it's Zhao Kang's.

choices.text: Give him the token

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: That's why people follow you, you know.

choices.text: Hand it to the elders to decide

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: Rules, rules. Fine. You're right. Again.

choices.text: Keep it

reply.speaker: rival_zhao
reply.text: (quietly) That was cold, {player}. Even for a war.

quests.title: The Hermit's Tea, Returned
quests.summary: On the way back you stop at the hermit's hut to return his cup. He looks at the seed in your hand for a long time.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: The warden gave you a seed. Three hundred years it held that seed. It never gave it to anyone.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: Do you know what it is?

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: I know what it will be. Not what it is. Plant it when you have a home that deserves it. Not before.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: And go home, child. Your Sect Master is waking. Even I can feel it, all the way out here.

dialogue.speaker: senior_wei
dialogue.text: I left the rest of the tea with the hermit. He cried. Just a bit. I think it was the tea. It's very strong.

quests.title: The Door Opens
quests.summary: Home at last, you find the gold seal torn from the main hall doors. The Sect Master has emerged, and she has read every letter.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: She's out. This morning. She read your report and Han Xue's four pages of please.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Before you see her, sit. The grotto shook your qi loose. Settle it, or you'll wobble in front of the Sect Master.

objectives.text: Settle the grotto's qi on the stone bridge

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The silver qi of the grotto settles into your meridians like snow into a valley. Great Perfection of Qi Condensation, clear and full.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Better. She'll send for you tomorrow. She has questions about Qingshi, and the deacon, and friends in high halls.

dialogue.speaker: elder_mo
dialogue.text: Tonight, eat. Sleep. Tomorrow you'll need both.

bonus.note: Grateful people press medicine into your hands.
Frightened people pay you to go away. You take it.
The Law Hall records your conduct with approval.
Rules bent, lessons learned the hard way.

quests.title: Missing Pages
quests.summary: The Sect Master wants to know everything about the Blood Moon Sect. Elder Bai's records should help. Should.

dialogue.speaker: master_yun
dialogue.text: A Blood Moon deacon, three hundred stolen hearts, and a hint of friends in high halls. I will not sleep tonight.

dialogue.speaker: master_yun
dialogue.text: Three centuries ago our founder and the Verdant Lotus Sect sealed the Blood Moon Patriarch beneath the Abyss.

dialogue.speaker: master_yun
dialogue.text: Elder Bai keeps the records. Learn how the seal was made, {player}. If it is failing, I must know why.

objectives.text: Ask Elder Bai for the Blood Moon records

dialogue.speaker: elder_bai
dialogue.text: The Blood Moon War chronicles? Fourth floor, east shelf, beside the recipes for turtle soup. Do not ask.

dialogue.speaker: elder_bai
dialogue.text: Here... hm. Hm! The pages on the Azure Heaven Seal are gone. Cut out. With a very sharp, very tidy blade.

dialogue.speaker: elder_bai
dialogue.text: Only elders and the Law Hall may enter the fourth floor. Whoever did this had a pass, and patience.

dialogue.speaker: elder_bai
dialogue.text: The Verdant Lotus built the seal. Their ruins lie in the Whispering Bamboo. Stones cannot be cut out of a book.

objectives.text: Watch the journey to the forgotten ruins
Find the gate of the ancient ruins

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: A stone archway rises from the bamboo, choked with vines. Carved lotus flowers climb its pillars.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: At its keystone is a single lotus, exactly the shape of the jade at your belt.

quests.title: The Hermit's Secret
quests.summary: The archway will not open for you. The hermit who warned you about the ruins knows more than he admits.

dialogue.speaker: narrator
dialogue.text: The hermit sits outside with two cups of tea already poured. He does not look surprised to see you.

objectives.text: Ask the hermit about the ruins

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: You went to the ruins. Of course you did. The young never listen and the old never stop talking.

dialogue.speaker: player
dialogue.text: The keystone matches my pendant. You knew. The first time you saw it, you knew.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: I did. Sit down. This tea has waited three hundred years. It can wait for one more story.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: My name is Lan Jue. Last disciple of the Verdant Lotus Sect. I ran when my masters died. I have been running ever since.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
dialogue.text: Your pendant is the Lotus Key, half of what binds the Azure Heaven Seal. Your mother was of our blood.

dialogue.speaker: hermit_lan
